title: Egress failover (BGP-less) handoff proposal and test plan
body:
Purpose:
- Capture a practical approach to provide deterministic egress failover for private deployments where customer environments do not support BGP or we choose not to run BGP.
- Surface terraform module changes, firewall mappings, DNS resolution behavior, and a staged cutover and rollback plan.

Background / constraints:
- Many onprem customers restrict peering and will not accept dynamic routing.
- We must preserve source identity for troubleshooting and compliance in some accounts, while for others SNAT is acceptable.
- Private DNS resolution must prefer local resolvers for internal hostnames, then fail over to a shared resolver in the event of gateway failover.
- Goal latency impact under 150ms for warm paths, and predictable re-route time under 60s for failover event.

Design options considered (summary):
1) Active-passive NAT gateway pair with health-probe and floating IP handed by cloud provider or customer load balancer.
   - Pros: simple, deterministic.
   - Cons: requires external IP reassignment capability, sometimes not allowed on netops side.
2) Egress proxy pair (reverse proxy or SOCKS) with client side retry and resolver pinning.
   - Pros: works without IP handoff, can preserve logical source headers.
   - Cons: adds app-proxy dependency and potential single point of failure if not scaled.
3) DNS-based failover with short TTLs and resolver delegation.
   - Pros: low infra change.
   - Cons: DNS cache coherence and long TTLs can delay recovery.
4) Source-NAT prefix translation and policy-based routing inside customer vpc, controlled via Terraform.
   - Pros: explicit control of source prefixes for upstream filters.
   - Cons: requires NAT allocation in both data centers and policy sync.

Our recommended hybrid approach (BGP-less):
- Primary mechanism: egress-proxy pair per region running in customer VPC or onprem cluster with health checks and automatic sidecar config distribution.
- Fallback mechanism: NAT gateway pair reachable via a managed floating VIP where customer permits, otherwise per-host SNAT.
- Resolver strategy: local resolver is first; proxy provides a forwarding resolver for upstream third-party DNS. When proxy fails, clients switch to a shared resolver endpoint using short TTLs and a resolver pin TTL of 10s on the agent.
- Firewall mapping: allow outbound to proxy VIPs on TCP 443 and 80, allow DNS UDP/53 to local resolver, allow DNS TCP/53 for fallback; limit source ranges to egress gateway subnets.

Terraform module notes (actionable):
- Add module: modules/egress-gateway with resources: compute instances, security group rules, healthcheck target group, autoscaling policy hooks, and optional floating_ip resource. Keep inputs minimal: desired_capacity, instance_type, allowed_outbound_cidrs, enable_floating_ip boolean.
- Introduce resource naming pattern: rw-egress-{env}-{region}-{role} to avoid collisions.
- State handling: store gateway state in separate tfstate backend per customer to avoid cross-tenant updates.
- Example variables to add to private-deployments/root module: egress.gateway_enabled, egress.proxy.image, egress.floating_ip_policy, dns.fallback_resolver.
- Migration helper: a small plan generator script that can map existing aws_nat_gateway resources to new egress-gateway resources and produce a patch plan in JSON. Place under infra/tools/egress-migrate.

Testing matrix and cutover plan (staged):
Stage 0: Canary sandbox
- Deploy egress-proxy to sandbox VPC. Update agent config to use proxy endpoint. Run traffic replay and verify headers, latency, and DNS resolution.
- Test scenarios: proxy kill, proxy restart, NAT-only path, DNS resolver failover, TTL expiry.

Stage 1: Non-critical customers
- Deploy with proxy in passive mode (no floating IP) and enable monitoring. Allow some customers to opt-in via feature flag.
- Smoke tests: outbound connectivity, allowed host list, packet capture sampling to verify SNAT behavior.

Stage 2: Partial cutover
- For customers that allow floating IPs, enable VIP failover with provider handoff and migrate small set of routes.
- Monitor metrics: 5xx rate, mean egress latency, DNS lookup times, connection reset counts.

Stage 3: Broad cutover
- Full switch with rollback window of 48 hours for each phase. Automated rollback trigger conditions: >2% 5xx, >=50% increase in median latency, DNS resolution failures >1%.

Rollback plan:
- Restore previous terraform state using state backend snapshot, reassign VIPs back to legacy NAT, and revert agent resolver pinning. Scripted rollback located at infra/scripts/egress_rollback.sh.

Observability and SLOs:
- Export metrics from proxy: connection_count, connect_latency_ms, upstream_error_count, dns_forward_latency_ms.
- Tagged metrics by customer_id, cluster, region.
- Set alerts for sustained error rate and DNS failure spikes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm customer policies about floating IP reassignments for top 10 customers. Ticketed in JIRA-INFRA-4123.
- Decide whether to run proxy as privileged container (needs NET_ADMIN) or use host networking for performance. Tradeoffs: container portability vs tuning capability.
- Finalize terraform naming and module inputs. Create GH PR for modules/egress-gateway.

Notes to implementers:
- Keep TTLs low only for resolver fallbacks; avoid DNS storms by rate limiting agent re-resolution.
- Use a short jittered backoff for client failover attempts to avoid thundering herd.
- Where source identity must be preserved, prefer TCP header passthrough via proxy and annotate logs with original ip if not SNATting.

Appendix: quick terraform snippet suggestion to include in module variables (pseudocode):
- variable "enable_floating_ip" { type = bool default = false }
- resource "floating_ip" "egress_vip" { count = var.enable_floating_ip ? 1 : 0 ... }

End notes: this is a working sketch. Next steps: schedule sync with Solutions Eng and Network Ops, spin up a sandbox deployment, and open the infra module PR for review.
